title: The per-layer direction list is not the number of directions that were ablated
detects: An artefact whose `directions_per_layer` list disagrees with `num_directions`. The list counts the directions EXTRACTED and kept at each layer; the count says how many the saved model actually had removed. A list reading [3, 2, 1, 3] beside a count of 1 means three candidates were available at that layer and one was used. The list is the field a reader is most likely to quote and the one they are most likely to read as the edit.
incident: Ours, and the artefact already knows. `build_abliteration_record` carries a `directions_index_note` whose first sentence is THESE ARE THE DIRECTIONS EXTRACTED AND KEPT PER LAYER, NOT THE NUMBER ABLATED, written because the two routinely disagree and somebody had quoted the wrong one. A note in the artefact is a rule enforced by whoever reads the file to the end, which is the same shape as the `budget_warning` that was written into three artefacts and read by nobody, and as the 2026-09-02 layer-versus-position mix-up where one wrong noun produced three wrong published statements.
remedy: Quote `num_directions` with `dir_mode` when describing what the edit removed, and quote `directions_per_layer` only as what the search had available. If a write-up already names the list as the edit, the number in it is wrong wherever the two disagree, and which layers disagree is in the list itself.
false_positive: A run where the search used every direction it found produces a list that agrees with the count at every layer and stays quiet, so the quiet case is real. The noisy case is a run with a ceiling above one, where disagreement is the expected outcome of the search choosing its budget and is not a defect in the run at all. Medium confidence for that reason: this says a reader is standing in front of two numbers that mean different things, not that the run went wrong. It fires per artefact and cannot see whether anybody actually quoted the list, which is the thing that turns it into an error.
